method: Byte review, atomscan before/after, cleave facts, rizin disassembly, isolated Lua arithmetic/string decoding. ML classifications were treated as priors.

evidence: core.py locates Node.js and invokes gweb_wasm_signer.js with index-5ee0c009.js as an argv data path. It provides authentication state through stdin.
The signer reads the JS bundle as UTF-8, matches base64 WASM magic AGFzbQE, decodes the capture with Buffer.from, and instantiates the WASM with empty imports. It does not evaluate the JS bundle.

The bundle contains SweetAlert2 browser code gating pointerEvents=none and looping audio on navigator.language and Russian host suffixes. This remains a suspicious dormant code finding in the wheel, with notable identity and mechanics.
API endpoints, encryption, and token use support the user-requested authentication purpose; no credential theft or hidden host compromise was found.
samples.changes: Add general WASM text-extraction and Python argv/PATH capabilities; narrowly downgrade the regional routine in a Python/Node data-extraction archive without HTML or all-sites extension delivery; keep standalone browser impact hostile and identity notable.
controls: Standalone bundled JS retains one hostile regional routine.
Adding an HTML member referencing the bundled JS defeats the downgrade and restores hostile impact.
Computed Python/Node exception precision: 9.3; standalone regional impact precision: 7.6.
samples.dependencies: Fetched GitHub behaviors, code-view and app-runtime assets have no hostile or suspicious traits. The false positive belongs to the wheel context, not those dependencies.

evidence: At 0x401260 the program constructs a System32 StormServer.dll path and changes LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL using RegDeleteValueA and RegSetValueExA.
At 0x402460 it extracts an embedded PE resource with FindResource/SizeofResource/LoadResource/LockResource and writes the payload.
At 0x401150 it allocates/writes a DLL pathname into a created process, resolves LoadLibraryA and uses it as CreateRemoteThread start address. The carrier selector chooses calc/notepad/iexplore.
Storm ddos Server and Welcome to use storm ddos banners establish family identity in conjunction with the service hijack. The collector filename does not establish Remcos or WannaCry.
The extracted DLL resource is incomplete/zeroed at its code entry; no live DDoS functionality is claimed.
samples.changes: Require LanmanServer ServiceDLL registry writes for hostile injection; anchor StormAttack attribution to banners plus behavior rather than a mutable DLL basename. Move the resource text/html HTTP header out of embedded-media metadata into HTTP Content-Type capabilities.
controls: Replacing LanmanServer with a same-length unrelated service removes both revised hostile findings; the neutral remote-memory/LoadLibrary profile remains.
Changing StormServer.dll to a same-length arbitrary DLL name preserves both revised findings.
Computed precision: remote DLL injection 9.6; StormAttack composite 12.2.

samples.identity: MarketData source-package lure delivering a packed Lua Windows backdoor/loader
evidence: The nominal Go module contains placeholder Rust source and a nested ZIP advertised by misleading release-page/image links and download/run instructions.
Launcher.cmd runs reinit.exe icon.txt; reinit.exe is a renamed LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3 runtime, not independently malicious. icon.txt is a packed Lua VM program.

Pure Lua decoding was isolated from real OS, IO, network, native FFI and Python interfaces. Intercepted native calls hide the console and request RWX VirtualAlloc memory; execution stops at the allocation sink.

Recovered routines/configuration include Windows PEB export resolution, screen capture APIs, Wininet POST with host identification fields, Run/StartupApproved persistence, hidden PowerShell and scheduled-task commands, and C2 configuration. These hidden operations do not implement the advertised placeholder market-data processor.
Recovered network configuration includes http://213.176.73.160 and Polygon eth_call endpoints; no live C2 request was made. Attribution to a specific malware family is not established.
samples.changes: Packed Lua plus a data-file launcher and runtime is suspicious by itself. Retain two hostile deceptive-delivery findings on the outer archive, with accurate obfuscation findings on icon.txt.
samples.dependencies: serde_json 1.0.152 has no hostile or suspicious traits; no dependency-specific exception was needed.
controls: Computed hostile precision: image ZIP delivery 9.4; release-page deception 7.5.
cleave test-rules on the raw ZIP does not reproduce recursive archive aggregation; final atomscan recursive results are authoritative for matched archive findings.
The extracted LuaJIT runtime is retained as notable identity/capabilities; the nested archive alone has six suspicious findings and no hostile trait.

moves.reason: The match is an HTTP header in a resource, not evidence of an HTML document.
Co-occurrence supports packed Lua, a runtime and a data-file argument; it does not bind the executable identity to the launched argument.
